sentences.l: Given-to-solitude, eating-little, whose-speech-body-and-mind-are-controlled, intent-on-the-yoga-of-meditation, constantly, dispassion having-taken-refuge-in,
sentences.i: Living apart, eating sparingly, controlling speech, body, and mind, always absorbed in the yoga of meditation, taking refuge constantly in dispassion,
sentences.n: Continues the ascetic portrait: vivikta-sevī, 'given to solitude' (recalling 6.10's rahasi sthitaḥ ekākī), laghu-āśī, 'eating little' (echoing 6.16-17's yukta-āhāra-vihārasya), yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ, 'controlled in speech, body and mind', dhyāna-yoga-paraḥ, 'given over to the yoga of meditation', nityaṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ, 'constantly resorting to dispassion' (vairāgya paired with abhyāsa as the two pillars of practice at 6.35). The verse remains without a finite verb, continuing the chain of description begun in verse 51 and closed only in verse 53.

sentences.t:
अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ।
विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
sentences.tr:
ahaṃkāram balam darpam kāmam krodham parigraham |
vimucya nirmamaḥ śāntaḥ brahma-bhūyāya kalpate ||

morph.gloss: egotism, the sense of 'I' (acc. sg. masc., object of vimucya)
[aggressive] strength, force (acc. sg. neut., object)
arrogance, pride, conceit (acc. sg. masc., object)
desire (acc. sg. masc., object)
anger (acc. sg. masc., object)
possessiveness, grasping, acquisitiveness (acc. sg. masc., object)
to abandon, let go of (vimucya: gerund)
free from [the sense of] 'mine' (nom. sg. masc., predicate)
calm, at peace (śānta: past participle; nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ before b- → -o)
brahman, kept untranslated per convention (first member)
the state of becoming (abstract noun from bhū; brahma-bhūyāya: 'for the state of being brahman', dat. sg. of purpose)
to become fit for, be qualified for (kalpate: present middle 3rd sg.)

sentences.l: Egotism, [aggressive] force, arrogance, desire, anger, [and] possessiveness, having-let-go, free-from-'mine', at-peace — for-the-state-of-brahman he-becomes-fit.
sentences.i: Having let go of egotism, force, arrogance, desire, anger, and possessiveness, free from the sense of 'mine' and at peace, he becomes fit for identity with brahman.
sentences.n: Closes the chain of gerunds begun in verse 51 (niyamya, tyaktvā, vyudasya ... vimucya) with the finite verb kalpate, 'he becomes fit for': having given up ahaṃkāram, balam, darpam, kāmam, krodham, parigraham, 'egotism, [aggressive] force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness' — faults condemned individually elsewhere in the poem (ahaṃkāra at 3.27, kāma-krodha as the twin gate of hell at 16.21) — such a person, nirmamaḥ, 'free from "mine"', śāntaḥ, 'at peace', kalpate brahma-bhūyāya, 'becomes fit for the state of brahman', for identity with brahman. Brahman kept untranslated per convention; this state opens directly, in verse 54, into devotion to Kṛṣṇa himself.

sentences.t:
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥
sentences.tr:
brahma-bhūtaḥ prasanna-ātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu mad-bhaktim labhate parām ||

morph.gloss: brahman, kept untranslated per convention (first member)
become, having become (bhūta: past participle; brahma-bhūtaḥ: 'one with brahman', nom. sg. masc., subject)
serene, clear, tranquil (prasanna: past participle; first member)
self (prasanna-ātmā: 'whose self is serene', nom. sg. masc., predicate)
not
to grieve, sorrow (śocati: present 3rd sg.)
not
to desire, crave (kāṅkṣati: present 3rd sg.)
equal, the same [toward all] (nom. sg. masc., predicate)
all (loc. pl.)
a being (loc. pl., 'toward all beings')
my (first member, from aham)
devotion (mad-bhaktim: 'devotion to me', acc. sg. fem., object of labhate)
to obtain (labhate: present middle 3rd sg.)
supreme (parām: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with bhaktim)

sentences.l: One-with-brahman, whose-self-is-serene, he-does-not grieve, he-does-not crave; equal toward-all beings, devotion-to-me he-obtains, supreme.
sentences.i: One with brahman, his self serene, he neither grieves nor craves; equal toward all beings, he attains supreme devotion to me.
sentences.n: The pivot of the chapter's closing movement: brahma-bhūtaḥ, 'one who has become brahman' (the state just reached in verse 53), prasanna-ātmā, 'serene of self', is described exactly as the sthitaprajña was in chapter 2 (na śocati na kāṅkṣati recalls 2.57) and as equanimous as the ideal yogin of 6.29 (samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu). But rather than stopping at this impersonal attainment, Kṛṣṇa's teaching makes it the doorway to something further: mad-bhaktiṃ ... parām, 'supreme devotion to me' — knowledge of the impersonal absolute culminating not in mere liberation but in bhakti, devotion to the personal Lord, the poem's characteristic synthesis (cf. 7.19's vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti, 14.26-27's brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāham).

sentences.t:
भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः ।
ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ॥
sentences.tr:
bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaḥ ca asmi tattvataḥ |
tataḥ mām tattvataḥ jñātvā viśate tat anantaram ||

morph.gloss: devotion (instr. sg., 'through devotion')
I (mām: acc. sg., object of abhijānāti)
to know fully, recognize (abhijānāti: present 3rd sg.; simply joined, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
how great, how much (yāvān: nom. sg. masc. relative, predicate)
who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative, predicate; -aḥ+c- → -aś c-)
and
to be (asmi: present 1st sg.; ca+asmi → cāsmi, a+a → ā)
truth, reality (tattvataḥ: ablative-adverbial, 'truly, in reality')
then, thereafter (adverb; -aḥ before m- → -o)
I (mām: acc. sg., object of jñātvā)
truth (tattvataḥ: ablative-adverbial, 'truly'; -aḥ before j- → -o)
to know (jñātvā: gerund, 'having known')
to enter (viśate: present middle 3rd sg.)
that (tat: acc. sg. neut. used adverbially; simply joined, dental+a, no change)
immediately following (anantaram: adverbial acc., 'immediately thereafter')

sentences.l: Through-devotion he-recognizes me, how-great and-who I-am, truly; then, me, truly, having-known, he-enters immediately-thereafter.
sentences.i: Through devotion he comes to know me truly, how great I am and who I am; and having known me in truth, he enters into me directly.
sentences.n: Explains how the supreme devotion just named (verse 54) itself becomes the means to final knowledge: bhaktyā mām abhijānāti, 'through devotion he comes to know me', yāvān yaḥ ca asmi tattvataḥ, 'how great and who I truly am' (echoing 7.1's yathā māṃ ... jñāsyasi and 10.7's yo vetti tattvataḥ) — devotion, not abstract reasoning, is what finally delivers real knowledge of Kṛṣṇa's nature. Viśate tad-anantaram, 'he enters immediately thereafter', promises the most intimate result the poem offers: not mere approach to Kṛṣṇa but entry into him.

sentences.t:
सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः ।
मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥
sentences.tr:
sarva-karmāṇi api sadā kurvāṇaḥ mad-vyapāśrayaḥ |
mat-prasādāt avāpnoti śāśvatam padam avyayam ||

morph.gloss: all (first member)
action (sarva-karmāṇi: 'all actions', acc. pl. neut., object of kurvāṇaḥ)
even, though (sarvakarmāṇi+api → sarvakarmāṇyapi, -i+a- → -y a-)
always
doing (kurvāṇa: present middle participle; nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ before m- → -o)
me (first member, from aham)
taking refuge in, dependent on (mad-vyapāśrayaḥ: 'having me as refuge', nom. sg. masc., predicate)
my (first member)
grace, favor (mat-prasādāt: 'through my grace', abl. sg.)
to obtain, reach (avāpnoti: present 3rd sg.; simply joined, dental+a, no change)
eternal (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with padam)
state, station, abode (padam: acc. sg. neut., object of avāpnoti)
imperishable (avyayam: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with padam; simply joined, final -m unaffected before the vowel)

sentences.l: All-actions even, always, doing, having-me-as-refuge; through-my-grace, he-obtains the-eternal imperishable state.
sentences.i: Even while performing all actions at all times, taking refuge in me, he obtains, through my grace, the eternal, imperishable state.
sentences.n: Closes the section begun at verse 49 with the poem's characteristic reconciliation: sarva-karmāṇi api sadā kurvāṇaḥ, 'even performing all actions always', continued action is no obstacle at all once mad-vyapāśrayaḥ, 'taking me as refuge' — the same teaching that opened the chapter's own argument against outright renunciation (verses 5-6, 9). Mat-prasādāt, 'through my grace', names the means by which the śāśvataṃ padam avyayam, 'the eternal, imperishable state' (echoing 8.21's paramaṃ padam and 15.6's paramaṃ mama dhāma), is finally reached — not by the seeker's effort alone — closing the thought before Kṛṣṇa's direct call to surrender begins at verse 57.

sentences.t:
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः ।
बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥
sentences.tr:
cetasā sarva-karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya mat-paraḥ |
buddhi-yogam upāśritya mat-cittaḥ satatam bhava ||

morph.gloss: mind, thought (instr. sg., 'with [your] mind')
all (first member)
action (sarva-karmāṇi: 'all actions', acc. pl. neut., object of saṃnyasya)
I (mayi: loc. sg., 'in me')
to lay down, deposit, entrust (saṃnyasya: gerund, 'having entrusted')
me (first member, from aham)
devoted to, intent on, having as one's highest (mat-paraḥ: 'devoted to me', nom. sg. masc., predicate)
intellect (first member)
yoga, kept untranslated per convention (buddhi-yogam: 'the yoga of the intellect', acc. sg. masc., object of upāśritya)
to resort to, take refuge in (upāśritya: gerund; simply joined, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
me (first member)
mind, thought (mat-cittaḥ: 'whose mind is on me', nom. sg. masc., predicate; mad+cittaḥ → maccittaḥ, -d+c- → -c c-)
constantly, always (adverb)
to be (bhava: imperative 2nd sg., 'be!')

sentences.l: With-[your]-mind, all-actions, in-me, having-entrusted, devoted-to-me; the-yoga-of-the-intellect having-resorted-to, whose-mind-is-on-me, constantly, be.
sentences.i: With your mind, entrust all your actions to me, holding me as the highest; resorting to the yoga of the intellect, keep your thought fixed on me always.
sentences.n: Opens the chapter's closing sequence on surrender (verses 57-62), turning from third-person description (verses 49-56) to Kṛṣṇa's direct second-person address. Cetasā sarva-karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya, 'with your mind entrusting all actions to me' — saṃnyasya, from the same root as saṃnyāsa, the very word defined at the chapter's start (verse 2), now recast as an inward act of dedication rather than outward abstention. Buddhi-yogam upāśritya, 'resorting to the yoga of the intellect' (first named at 2.49), and mat-cittaḥ satatam bhava, 'be one whose mind is on me constantly' (echoing 8.7's mām anusmara yudhya ca), restate the whole poem's teaching in its most direct imperative form.

sentences.t:
मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि ।
अथ चेत्त्वमहंकारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥
sentences.tr:
mat-cittaḥ sarva-durgāṇi mat-prasādāt tariṣyasi |
atha cet tvam ahaṃkārāt na śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi ||

morph.gloss: me (first member)
mind (mat-cittaḥ: 'whose mind is on me', nom. sg. masc., subject, 'you')
all (first member)
a difficulty, a danger, an obstacle (sarva-durgāṇi: acc. pl. neut., object of tariṣyasi)
my (first member)
grace (mat-prasādāt: 'through my grace', abl. sg.; simply joined with the following word, dental+dental)
to cross over (tariṣyasi: future 2nd sg.)
but, now
if (cet: conditional particle; simply joined with tvam, dental+dental)
you (tvam: nom. sg., subject)
egotism (ahaṃkārāt: abl. sg., 'out of egotism'; simply joined with na, dental+dental)
not
to hear, heed (śroṣyasi: future 2nd sg.)
to be lost, to perish (vinaṅkṣyasi: future 2nd sg.)

sentences.l: Whose-mind-is-on-me, all-difficulties, through-my-grace, you-will-cross; but if you, out-of-egotism, will-not heed, you-will-perish.
sentences.i: With your mind fixed on me, you will cross over every difficulty through my grace; but if out of egotism you do not heed this, you will perish.
sentences.n: States both the promise (mat-prasādāt sarva-durgāṇi tariṣyasi, 'through my grace you will cross every difficulty') and the warning (ahaṃkārāt na śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi, 'if out of egotism you do not heed this, you will be lost') framing Kṛṣṇa's call to surrender — the same ahaṃkāra already condemned throughout the chapter (verses 17, 24, 53) now named as the one thing capable of blocking it.

sentences.t:
यदहंकारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे ।
मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति ॥
sentences.tr:
yat ahaṃkāram āśritya na yotsye iti manyase |
mithyā eṣaḥ vyavasāyaḥ te prakṛtiḥ tvām niyokṣyati ||

morph.gloss: which, as to which (yat: acc. sg. neut. used adverbially; yat+ahaṃkāram → yadahaṃkāram, -t+a- → -d a-)
egotism (ahaṃkāram: acc. sg. masc., object of āśritya)
to resort to, rely on (āśritya: gerund)
not
to fight (yotsye: future middle 1st sg., 'I will fight'; realized yotsya before the following iti, as already noted at 2.9)
thus (closing the quoted thought)
to think (manyase: present middle 2nd sg.)
falsely, in vain (adverb)

this (eṣaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; mithyā+eṣaḥ → mithyaiṣaḥ, ā+e → ai; eṣaḥ's own visarga then drops before the following v-, a standing exception for the pronouns sa/eṣa before any consonant, already noted at 17.11)
resolve, determination (vyavasāya: nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ+t- → -as t-)
your (te: gen. sg.)
nature (nom. sg. fem., subject; -iḥ+t- → -is t-)
you (tvām: acc. sg., object of niyokṣyati)
to engage, compel, yoke (niyokṣyati: future 3rd sg.)

sentences.l: As-to-which, relying-on-egotism, 'I-will-not fight' — thus you-think — vain [is] this resolve-of-yours; [your-own] nature will-compel you.
sentences.i: If, relying on egotism, you think 'I will not fight' — this resolve of yours is vain; your own nature will compel you.
sentences.n: Returns to the poem's opening crisis, quoting almost verbatim Arjuna's own resolve at 2.9's na yotsya iti — there his despair, here named ahaṃkāra, egotism. Mithyā eṣa vyavasāyaḥ te, 'this resolve of yours is false', and prakṛtiḥ tvāṃ niyokṣyati, 'your own nature will compel you', anticipate verse 60's fuller argument that a kṣatriya's inborn nature makes his fighting inevitable regardless of his private wishes.

sentences.t:
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा ।
कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् ॥
sentences.tr:
svabhāva-jena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā |
kartum na icchasi yat mohāt kariṣyasi avaśaḥ api tat ||

morph.gloss: one's own nature (first member)
born of (svabhāva-jena: 'born of your own nature', instr. sg., agreeing with karmaṇā)
son of Kuntī, Arjuna (vocative)
bound (nibaddha: past participle; nom. sg. masc., predicate)
one's own (instr. sg.)
action (instr. sg., 'by [your own] duty')
to do (kartum: infinitive, complementing icchasi)
not
to wish (icchasi: present 2nd sg.; na+icchasi → necchasi, a+i → e)
which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, object of icchasi and kariṣyasi; yat+mohāt → yanmohāt, -t+m- → -n m-)
delusion (mohāt: abl. sg., 'out of delusion')
to do (kariṣyasi: future 2nd sg.; kariṣyasi+avaśaḥ → kariṣyasyavaśaḥ, -i+a- → -y a-)
not in [one's own] control, helpless (avaśaḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate agreeing with 'you'; avaśaḥ+api → avaśo'pi, -aḥ+a- → -o' with avagraha)
even
that (acc. sg. neut., resuming yat)

sentences.l: Bound by-[your-own]-duty, born-of-[your-own]-nature, Kaunteya, which, out-of-delusion, you-do-not wish to-do — that, powerless, you-will-do, even against-your-will.
sentences.i: Bound by your own duty, born of your own nature, Kaunteya, what you, out of delusion, do not wish to do — that you will do anyway, helplessly, even against your will.
sentences.n: Closes the argument begun in verse 59: nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā svabhāva-jena, 'bound by your own duty, born of your own nature' (the same svabhāva-niyataṃ karma praised at verse 47, now shown to bind whether one likes it or not), means that yat mohāt kartum na icchasi, 'what, out of delusion, you do not wish to do', tat kariṣyasi avaśaḥ api, 'you will do anyway, even helplessly' — an almost deterministic close to the poem's long argument for freely embracing one's duty: nature will have its way regardless, so wisdom lies in consenting to it rather than resisting.

sentences.t:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति ।
भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥
sentences.tr:
īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānām hṛt-deśe arjuna tiṣṭhati |
bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni yantra-ārūḍhāni māyayā ||

morph.gloss: the Lord, the [supreme] controller (nom. sg. masc., subject)
all (first member)
a being (sarva-bhūtānām: 'of all beings', gen. pl.)
heart (first member)
place, region (hṛt-deśe: 'in the region of the heart', loc. sg.; hṛddeśe+arjuna → hṛddeśe'rjuna, -e+a- → -e' with avagraha)
Arjuna (vocative)
to stand, dwell, abide (tiṣṭhati: present 3rd sg.)
causing to revolve, whirling (causative present participle bhrāmayant; bhrāmayan: nom. sg. masc.)
all (first member)
a being (sarva-bhūtāni: acc. pl. neut., object of bhrāmayan)
a machine, a mechanical device (first member)
mounted upon, set upon (ārūḍha: past participle; yantra-ārūḍhāni: 'mounted on a machine', acc. pl. neut., agreeing with sarvabhūtāni; yantra+ārūḍhāni → yantrārūḍhāni, a+ā → ā)
illusion, [the Lord's] creative power (instr. sg., 'by [his] māyā')

sentences.l: The-Lord, of-all-beings, in-the-region-of-the-heart, Arjuna, dwells, causing-to-revolve all-beings, mounted-on-a-machine, by-[his]-māyā.
sentences.i: The Lord dwells in the heart-region of all beings, Arjuna, whirling them about, as if mounted on a machine, by his māyā.
sentences.n: The chapter's most vivid image of divine immanence and control: īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ hṛd-deśe tiṣṭhati, 'the Lord dwells in the heart-region of all beings' (recalling 13.17's sarvasya ca hṛdi sthitam and 15.15's sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭaḥ), bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni yantra-ārūḍhāni māyayā, 'whirling all beings about, as though mounted on a machine, through māyā' — the machine (yantra), perhaps a water-wheel or puppet-mechanism, a striking image for the compulsion just described in verse 60: beings, seemingly autonomous, are moved by their own nature under the Lord's governance, exactly as māyā was said to operate at 7.14.

sentences.t:
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत ।
तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥
sentences.tr:
tam eva śaraṇam gaccha sarva-bhāvena bhārata |
tat-prasādāt parām śāntim sthānam prāpsyasi śāśvatam ||

morph.gloss: him (tam: acc. sg. masc., object of gaccha, referring to īśvaraḥ)
alone, only (simply joined, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
refuge, shelter (acc. sg. neut., object of gaccha)
to go (gaccha: imperative 2nd sg., 'go!')
whole, entire (first member)
being, disposition (sarva-bhāvena: 'with your whole being', instr. sg. used adverbially)
descendant of Bharata, Arjuna (vocative)
his (first member)
grace (tat-prasādāt: 'through his grace', abl. sg.; simply joined with the following word, dental+p)
supreme (parām: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with śāntim)
peace (acc. sg. fem., object of prāpsyasi)

eternal (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with sthānam)

sentences.l: Him alone, as-refuge, go, with-[your]-whole-being, Bhārata; through-his-grace, supreme peace, [and] the-eternal abode, you-will-attain.
sentences.i: Go to him alone as your refuge, Bhārata, with your whole being; through his grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
sentences.n: Closes the surrender sequence (verses 57-62) with a direct command anticipating verse 66's famous mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja: tam eva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarva-bhāvena, 'go to him alone as refuge, with your whole being' — tam, 'him', referring back to īśvaraḥ of verse 61, i.e. Kṛṣṇa. Tat-prasādāt parāṃ śāntiṃ sthānaṃ ... śāśvatam, 'through his grace, supreme peace and the eternal abode', promises exactly what mat-prasādāt promised at verses 56 and 58 — grace as the means, not the seeker's unaided effort.

sentences.t:
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया ।
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
sentences.tr:
iti te jñānam ākhyātam guhyāt guhyataram mayā |
vimṛśya etat aśeṣeṇa yathā icchasi tathā kuru ||

morph.gloss: thus (marking the close of the teaching just given)
to you (dat. sg.)

to declare, tell (ākhyāta: past participle; nom. sg. neut., predicate, 'has been declared')
secret (guhyāt: abl. sg., standard of comparison)

sentences.l: Thus, to-you, knowledge has-been-declared, more-secret than-[what-is]-secret, by-me; having-considered this fully, as you-wish, so do.
sentences.i: Thus I have declared to you knowledge more secret than any secret; reflect on this fully, and then do as you wish.
sentences.n: A pivotal verse pausing before the chapter's final, most confidential teaching (verses 64-66): guhyād guhyataram, 'more secret than [what is] secret' (echoing 9.1's guhyatamaṃ and anticipating verse 64's sarva-guhyatamam, 'the most secret of all'), names what has just been taught (the surrender of verses 57-62) as already exceptionally confidential. Vimṛśya etat aśeṣeṇa yathā icchasi tathā kuru, 'having considered this fully, do as you wish', is one of the poem's most striking moments: after everything, Kṛṣṇa explicitly leaves the final choice to Arjuna's own judgment and free will, refusing to compel assent even at the climax of his teaching.

sentences.t:
सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥

iṣṭaḥ asi me dṛḍham iti tataḥ vakṣyāmi te hitam ||

sentences.l: The-most-secret-of-all, again, hear my supreme word: 'you-are dear to-me, firmly' — thus; therefore I-will-speak to-you [your] good.
sentences.i: Hear again my supreme word, the most secret of all: you are truly dear to me — and so I will tell you what is good for you.
sentences.n: Introduces the chapter's very last and most confidential teaching (verses 65-66), building past verse 63's guhyād guhyataram to sarva-guhyatamam, 'the most secret of all'. Iṣṭaḥ asi me dṛḍham iti, 'you are firmly dear to me', gives Kṛṣṇa's own stated motive for the final revelation about to come — not obligation but personal affection for Arjuna — and vakṣyāmi te hitam, 'I will tell you what is good for you', promises the poem's last piece of practical counsel before its climax in verse 66.

sentences.t:

मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥

sentences.l: Whose-mind-is-on-me be, my-devotee, worshipping-me; me do-homage-to; me-alone you-will-come-to — truly, to-you I-promise; dear you-are to-me.
sentences.i: Fix your mind on me, be my devotee, worship me, bow down to me; you will come to me alone — this I promise you truly, for you are dear to me.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa's final personal appeal before the summary verse 66: man-manāḥ, mad-bhaktaḥ, mad-yājī, mām namaskuru, 'fix your mind on me, be my devotee, worship me, bow down to me' — the same fourfold formula already given almost verbatim at 9.34, now repeated at the chapter's climax to bracket the poem's teaching on devotion. Mām eva eṣyasi, 'you will come to me alone', satyaṃ te pratijāne, 'I promise you this is true' — Kṛṣṇa's direct personal guarantee, grounded in priyaḥ asi me, 'you are dear to me', the same bond of affection just named in verse 64.

sentences.t:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।
अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥

aham tvām sarva-pāpebhyaḥ mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ ||

all (first member)

sentences.l: All dharmas having abandoned, to me alone as refuge come; I you from all evils will free — do not grieve.
sentences.i: Let go of every duty and come to me as your one refuge. I will free you from all evil; do not grieve.
sentences.n: The poem's single most famous verse, traditionally called the carama-śloka, 'final verse [of the teaching]', summing up the whole Gītā in two lines: sarva-dharmān parityajya, 'having abandoned all dharmas' (every dharma whatsoever — not only one's own sva-dharma, so intently argued for earlier in this very chapter, but the whole edifice of duty), mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja, 'come to me alone as refuge' — the culmination of the surrender already urged at verses 57 and 62. Vulgate reads tvāṃ, the ordinary accusative of 'you'; the BORI critical edition reads tvā, an older enclitic accusative form of the same pronoun, identical in sense — a real vulgate/BORI variant, not adopted here but noted. Mā śucaḥ, 'do not grieve', closes the verse by answering Arjuna's very first named affliction (śoka, cf. 2.1's śoka-saṃvigna-mānasam) with Kṛṣṇa's final personal reassurance. This verse's l and i follow the house rendering fixed in conventions.md, drafted fresh from the Sanskrit rather than from any modern published translation, given its extraordinary fame: sarva-dharmān is rendered 'all dharmas' in l (dharma kept visible as the technical term) and 'every duty' in i, per the house text.

न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥

sentences.l: This, by-you, [is] not-to-be-told to-one-without-austerity, ever, nor to-a-non-devotee, nor to-one-unwilling-to-hear, nor to-whoever is-malicious toward-me.
sentences.i: This is not to be told by you to one without discipline, ever, nor to one who is not a devotee, nor to one unwilling to hear it, nor to anyone who is spiteful toward me.
sentences.n: Opens the chapter's closing instructions on the confidentiality of the teaching (verses 67-71), naming four kinds of unfit hearer: a-tapaskāya, 'to one without austerity/self-discipline'; a-bhaktāya, 'to a non-devotee'; a-śuśrūṣave, 'to one unwilling to listen respectfully'; and yaḥ mām abhyasūyati, 'whoever is spiteful toward me' (the same malice named of hostile critics elsewhere, cf. 3.32, 9.3's aśraddadhānāḥ). Idaṃ te ... na vācyam, 'this is not to be told by you', uses a dative of agent with the gerundive vācyam, a recognized Sanskrit construction.

भक्तिं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः ॥

sentences.l: Who this supreme secret, among-my-devotees, will-declare, having-shown supreme devotion toward-me, to-me-alone he-will-come, without-doubt.
sentences.i: Whoever declares this supreme secret among my devotees, having shown supreme devotion toward me, will come to me alone, without doubt.
sentences.n: Promises the reward for transmitting the teaching, the positive counterpart to verse 67's restriction: mad-bhakteṣu abhidhāsyati, 'declares it among my devotees' — the correct audience implied negatively there now stated positively. Vulgate reads imam, an alternative masculine-pattern accusative singular of idam agreeing with guhyam by sense rather than strict gender; the BORI critical edition reads the more regular neuter idam, agreeing directly with guhyam — a real vulgate/BORI variant in form only, not a difference of sense, not adopted here but noted. Mām eva eṣyati asaṃśayaḥ, 'he will come to me alone, without doubt', echoes verse 65's identical promise (mām eva eṣyasi satyaṃ), now extended to the teacher of the teaching as well as to its original recipient.

sentences.t:

भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥

sentences.i: And there is no one among human beings who does me more dear service than he; nor will anyone else on earth be dearer to me than he.
sentences.n: Ranks the teacher of verse 68 above all others in Kṛṣṇa's regard: kaścit me priya-kṛttamaḥ, 'anyone more dear-service-doing to me' (priya-kṛttama, a superlative naming the highest degree of pleasing service), na bhavitā, 'nor will there be', tasmāt anyaḥ priyataraḥ bhuvi, 'anyone else dearer on earth'. The double negative (na ... na ca) presses the claim from both present and future.

sentences.n: Extends the promise beyond the original teacher/disciple pair to future students of the text itself: adhyeṣyate ... yaḥ imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādam āvayoḥ, 'whoever will study this righteous dialogue of ours' — the Gītā's own dialogue, referred to here within itself. Jñāna-yajñena, 'by the sacrifice of knowledge' (echoing 4.33's ranking of jñāna-yajña above material sacrifice), tena aham iṣṭaḥ syām iti me matiḥ, 'by that I would be worshipped, in my view' — mere study of the teaching, undertaken in that spirit, itself counts as worship.

sentences.i: And even a man who merely hears it, with faith and without malice, is freed as well, and attains the fair worlds of those of virtuous deeds.
sentences.n: Closes the confidentiality section (verses 67-71) by extending the promise to the simplest possible engagement with the teaching: śraddhāvān an-asūyaḥ ... yaḥ naraḥ śṛṇuyāt api, 'even a man who merely hears it, with faith and without malice' (an-asūyaḥ directly answering verse 67's warning against yaḥ mām abhyasūyati, 'whoever is spiteful toward me'), saḥ api muktaḥ, 'he too is freed', reaching śubhān lokān puṇya-karmaṇām, 'the fair worlds of those of virtuous deeds' — a lesser but still substantial reward for the listener alone, below the teacher's promise of coming to Kṛṣṇa himself at verse 68. This closes the run of promises begun at verse 68, before Kṛṣṇa turns, in verse 72, to ask Arjuna directly whether the teaching has taken hold.

sentences.l: Has-this been-heard, Pārtha, by-you, with-one-pointed mind? Has-the-delusion-of-ignorance been-destroyed, of-yours, Dhanañjaya?
sentences.i: Has this been heard by you, Pārtha, with a one-pointed mind? Has the delusion born of ignorance been destroyed for you, Dhanañjaya?
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa's own question, closing the teaching before Arjuna's final reply (verse 73): kaccit etat śrutam tvayā eka-agreṇa cetasā, 'has this been heard by you with a one-pointed mind?' — echoing the concentration urged throughout (e.g. 6.12's ekāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā) — and kaccit ajñāna-saṃmohaḥ pranaṣṭaḥ te, 'has the delusion of ignorance been destroyed for you?', asking directly whether the very saṃmoha that opened the poem (cf. 1.30) has been dispelled by everything taught since. This personal check-in, rare in the poem's structure, marks the teaching as essentially complete.

sentences.l: Destroyed, [my] delusion; memory regained, by-me, through-your-grace, Acyuta; established I-am, my-doubt-gone; I-will-do [your] word, yours.
sentences.i: My delusion is destroyed; I have regained memory through your grace, Acyuta. I stand firm, my doubts gone; I will act on your word.
sentences.n: Arjuna's final response closes his own arc of the poem: naṣṭo mohaḥ, 'delusion is destroyed', directly answers Kṛṣṇa's question at verse 72. Smṛtir labdhā, 'memory has been regained' (recalling smṛti-bhraṃśa, 'the loss of memory', the last stage of desire's ruin named at 2.63), names the recovery of Arjuna's own clear understanding of his duty, obscured since chapter 1's grief. Sthitaḥ asmi gata-sandehaḥ, 'I am established, my doubt gone', and kariṣye vacanaṃ tava, 'I will act on your word', give Arjuna's own resolution — not mere intellectual agreement but a stated commitment to act, closing the frame-question of renunciation-versus-action with which the chapter itself began. Acyuta, 'the unfallen', an epithet of Kṛṣṇa (cf. 1.21).

sentences.i: Thus have I heard this wondrous, hair-raising dialogue between Vāsudeva and the great-souled Pārtha.
sentences.n: Sañjaya's own voice returns after the dialogue proper ends, opening the chapter's closing frame (verses 74-78), which mirrors the poem's opening frame in chapter 1. Vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahā-ātmanaḥ, 'of Vāsudeva and of the great-souled Pārtha', names both speakers by patronymic: Vāsudeva, 'son of Vasudeva', an epithet of Kṛṣṇa; Pārtha, 'son of Pṛthā', Arjuna. Adbhutam, 'wondrous', roma-harṣaṇam, 'hair-raising' (the same physical response to awe already described at 1.29 and throughout chapter 11's theophany, e.g. 11.14), names Sañjaya's own reaction as witness.

sentences.n: Sañjaya names the source of his own extraordinary knowledge: vyāsa-prasādāt, 'through the grace of Vyāsa' (the sage traditionally credited with composing the whole Mahābhārata, said to have granted Sañjaya the divine sight to witness the distant battlefield), enabling him to hear etat guhyam param, 'this supreme secret', yogam, 'yoga' — the poem's whole teaching named simply as yoga at its very close — sākṣāt, 'directly, in person', from yoga-īśvarāt kṛṣṇāt, 'from Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of yoga' (echoing 11.4's yogeśvara), kathayataḥ svayam, 'speaking it himself'. This closes the chain of transmission the chapter has traced since verse 70's teacher-to-student promise.

Saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya, 'remembering again and again' (a doubled gerund for repeated action, in the manner of yadā yadā at 4.7), and hṛṣyāmi ... muhur muhuḥ, 'I thrill again and again', name Sañjaya's own continuing rapture at having witnessed the dialogue; puṇyam, 'sacred, holy', echoes adbhutam of verse 74. Vismayaḥ ... mahān, 'great astonishment', and hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ, 'I thrill again and again' (echoing verse 76's muhur muhuḥ), close the personal reflection before the poem's final verse turns from Sañjaya's own feeling to a formal blessing. sentences.i: Where Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of yoga, is, and where Pārtha, the archer, is — there, I am convinced, are splendor, victory, prosperity, and firm right conduct.
sentences.n: The Gītā's closing verse, Sañjaya's own final judgment rather than any word of Kṛṣṇa or Arjuna: yatra yoga-īśvaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ, yatra pārthaḥ dhanur-dharaḥ, 'where Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of yoga, is, where Pārtha, the bow-bearer, is' — naming Kṛṣṇa by the same epithet just used at verse 75 and Arjuna by his warrior's role. Tatra śrīḥ vijayaḥ bhūtiḥ dhruvā nītiḥ, 'there splendor, victory, prosperity, and firm right conduct', names four goods together — dhruvā, 'firm, sure', may modify nīti alone or, more likely, the whole preceding list. Matir mama, 'this is my conviction', closes the entire eighteen-chapter poem not with a divine pronouncement but with the narrator's own considered judgment — Sañjaya, the once-neutral reporter of chapter 1, ending as a believer.

glossary.सात्त्विकं: sāttvikam — sāttvika — sattva-natured (nom. sg. neut., predicate)

glossary.विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम्: viṣaya-indriya-saṃyogāt yat tat agre amṛta-upamam — viṣaya — a sense-object (first member); indriya — a sense-organ (second member; viṣaya+indriya → viṣayendriya, a+i → e, guṇa); saṃyoga — contact, conjunction (viṣaya-indriya-saṃyogāt: 'from the contact of sense-object and sense-organ', abl. sg.); yad — which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative, subject); tad — that (tat: nom. sg. neut., resumptive correlative; dental+dental, written joined); agra — the beginning (agre: loc. sg. used adverbially, 'at first'; tat+agre → tadagre, -t+a- → -d a-); amṛta — nectar (first member; agre+amṛtopamam → agre'mṛtopamam, -e+a- → -e' with avagraha); upama — resembling, like (amṛta-upamam: 'like nectar', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
glossary.परिणामे: pariṇāme — pariṇāma — the outcome, the end, ripening (loc. sg. used adverbially, 'in the end')
glossary.स्मृतम्: smṛtam — smṛ — to remember, hold in mind (smṛta: past participle; nom. sg. neut., predicate, 'is held [to be]')
glossary.यदग्रे: yat agre — yad — which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative, subject); agra — the beginning (agre: loc. sg. used adverbially, 'at first'; yat+agre → yadagre, -t+a- → -d a-)
glossary.चानुबन्धे: ca anubandhe — ca — and (ca+anubandhe → cānubandhe, a+a → ā); anu-bandh — continuation, sequel (anubandha: loc. sg. used adverbially, 'thereafter, in what follows')
glossary.मोहनमात्मनः: mohanam ātmanaḥ — muh — deluding, stupefying (mohana: nom. sg. neut., predicate; simply joined with the following word, final -m unaffected before the vowel); ātman — self (ātmanaḥ: gen. sg., 'of the self')
glossary.निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं: nidrā-ālasya-pramāda-uttham — nidrā — sleep (first member); ālasya — laziness, indolence (second member; nidrā+ālasya → nidrālasya, ā+ā → ā); pramāda — negligence, heedlessness (third member); ud-sthā — arisen from, springing from (uttha: nom. sg. neut., agreeing with sukham; pramāda+uttham → pramādottham, a+u → o)
glossary.तदस्ति: tat asti — tad — that (tat: nom. sg. neut., subject; tat+asti → tadasti, -t+a- → -d a-); as — to be, exist (asti: present 3rd sg.)
glossary.दिवि: divi — div — heaven, sky (loc. sg., 'in heaven')
glossary.देवेषु: deveṣu — deva — a god (loc. pl., 'among the gods')
glossary.सत्त्वं: sattvam — sattva — a being, an existing thing (here the general sense of the word, not the guṇa named at length in this chapter — see note; nom. sg. neut., subject)
glossary.प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं: prakṛti-jaiḥ muktam — prakṛti — nature, primordial matter (first member); ja — born of (prakṛti-jaiḥ: 'born from nature', instr. pl. neut., agreeing with guṇaiḥ); muc — free, freed (mukta: past participle; muktam: nom. sg. neut., predicate agreeing with sattvam; -aiḥ+m- → -air m-)
glossary.यदेभिः: yat ebhiḥ — yad — which (yat: nom. sg. neut. relative, subject, resuming sattvam; yat+ebhiḥ → yadebhiḥ, -t+e- → -d e-); etad — these (ebhiḥ: instr. pl. neut., referring to guṇaiḥ)
glossary.स्यात्त्रिभिर्गुणैः: syāt tribhiḥ guṇaiḥ — as — to be (syāt: optative 3rd sg., 'would be'; simply joined, dental+t); tri — three (tribhiḥ: instr. pl.); guṇa — guṇa, kept untranslated per convention (guṇaiḥ: instr. pl.; -iḥ+g- → -ir g-)
glossary.ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां: brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-viśām — brāhmaṇa — a brahmin (first member); kṣatriya — a kṣatriya (second member); viś — a vaiśya, a commoner (brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-viśām: 'of brahmins, kṣatriyas and vaiśyas', gen. pl.)
glossary.शूद्राणां: śūdrāṇām — śūdra — a śūdra (gen. pl., 'and of śūdras')
glossary.परन्तप: parantapa — param-tap — scorcher of the foe, an epithet of Arjuna (vocative)
glossary.प्रविभक्तानि: pravibhaktāni — pra-vi-bhaj — divided, distributed, allotted (pravibhakta: past participle; nom. pl. neut., predicate)
glossary.स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः: svabhāva-prabhavaiḥ guṇaiḥ — sva-bhāva — one's own nature (first member); prabhava — arising from, born of (sva-bhāva-prabhavaiḥ: 'arising from [each one's] own nature', instr. pl., agreeing with guṇaiḥ); guṇa — guṇa, kept untranslated per convention (guṇaiḥ: instr. pl.; -aiḥ+g- → -air g-)
glossary.शमो: śamaḥ — śama — tranquility, calmness of mind (nom. sg. masc., list item; -aḥ before d- → -o)
glossary.दमस्तपः: damaḥ tapaḥ — dama — self-control, mastery of the senses (damaḥ: nom. sg. masc., list item; -aḥ+t- → -as t-); tapas — austerity (tapaḥ: nom. sg. neut., list item)
glossary.शौचं: śaucam — śauca — purity (nom. sg. neut., list item)
glossary.क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव: kṣāntiḥ ārjavam eva — kṣānti — patience, forbearance (kṣāntiḥ: nom. sg. fem., list item; -iḥ+ā- → -ir ā-); ārjava — uprightness, straightforwardness (ārjavam: nom. sg. neut., list item; simply joined with eva, final -m unaffected before the vowel); eva — too, indeed
glossary.विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं: vijñānam āstikyam — vi-jñāna — discernment, [experiential] insight (vijñānam: nom. sg. neut., list item; simply joined with the following word, final -m unaffected before the vowel); āstikya — faith [in scripture and the unseen], orthodoxy (āstikyam: nom. sg. neut., list item)
glossary.ब्रह्मकर्म: brahma-karma — brahman — here short for brāhmaṇa, 'brahmin' (not the metaphysical brahman kept untranslated elsewhere — see note; first member); karman — action (brahma-karma: 'the brahmin's duty', nom. sg. neut., subject)
glossary.स्वभावजम्: svabhāvajam — sva-bhāva — one's own nature (first member); ja — born of (sva-bhāva-jam: nom. sg. neut., predicate)
glossary.शौर्यं: śauryam — śaurya — heroism, valor (nom. sg. neut., list item)
glossary.तेजो: tejaḥ — tejas — vigor, fiery energy, splendor (nom. sg. neut., list item; -aḥ before dh- → -o)
glossary.धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं: dhṛtiḥ dākṣyam — dhṛti — steadfastness, firmness, resolve (dhṛtiḥ: nom. sg. fem., list item; -iḥ+d- → -ir d-); dākṣya — skill, competence, resourcefulness (dākṣyam: nom. sg. neut., list item)
glossary.चाप्यपलायनम्: ca api a-palāyanam — ca — and (ca+api → cāpi, a+a → ā); api — even, too; a-palāyana — not fleeing, non-flight (apalāyanam: nom. sg. neut., list item; api+apalāyanam → apyapalāyanam, -i+a- → -y a-)
glossary.दानमीश्वरभावश्च: dānam īśvara-bhāvaḥ ca — dāna — generosity, giving (dānam: nom. sg. neut., list item; simply joined with the following word, final -m unaffected before the vowel); īśvara — lordship, mastery (first member); bhāva — disposition, quality (īśvara-bhāvaḥ: 'a commanding disposition, the quality of lordship', nom. sg. masc., list item; -aḥ+c- → -aś c-); ca — and
glossary.क्षात्रं: kṣātram — kṣātra — belonging to the kṣatriya (adjective from kṣatra; nom. sg. neut., agreeing with karma — the vulgate reading, printed here, with kṣātra as a separate adjective; the BORI critical edition instead compounds the two as kṣatra-karma, 'kṣatriya-duty', the same sense reached as one word rather than two: a real vulgate/BORI variant, not a misprint; see the note)
glossary.कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं: kṛṣi-gau-rakṣya-vāṇijyam — kṛṣi — agriculture, farming (first member); go — a cow (here in the vulgate's spelling appearing as the nominative-like gau- before rakṣya rather than the ordinary compounding stem go- — see note); rakṣya — protection, tending (go-rakṣya: 'cattle-tending'); vāṇijya — trade, commerce (kṛṣi-gau-rakṣya-vāṇijyam: 'farming, cattle-tending and trade', nom. sg. neut., subject — the vulgate reading, printed here; the BORI critical edition reads the more regular kṛṣi-go-rakṣya-vāṇijyam, with the ordinary stem go-: a real vulgate/BORI variant in the compound's internal form, not a misprint and not a difference of sense; see the note)
glossary.वैश्यकर्म: vaiśya-karma — vaiśya — a vaiśya (first member); karman — action (vaiśya-karma: 'the vaiśya's duty', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
glossary.परिचर्यात्मकं: paricaryā-ātmakam — pari-caryā — service, attendance (first member); ātmaka — having the nature of, consisting in (paricaryā-ātmakam: 'consisting in service', nom. sg. neut., agreeing with karma)
glossary.शूद्रस्यापि: śūdrasya api — śūdra — a śūdra (śūdrasya: gen. sg., 'of the śūdra'); api — too, also (śūdrasya+api → śūdrasyāpi, a+a → ā)
glossary.स्वे: sve — sva — one's own (loc. sg. neut., 'in his own')
glossary.कर्मण्यभिरतः: karmaṇi abhirataḥ — karman — action (karmaṇi: loc. sg., 'in [his own] duty'); abhi-ram — devoted to, delighting in (abhirata: past participle; nom. sg. masc., predicate; karmaṇi+abhirataḥ → karmaṇyabhirataḥ, -i+a- → -y a-)
glossary.संसिद्धिं: saṃsiddhim — sam-sidh — accomplishment, success, perfection (acc. sg. fem., object of labhate)
glossary.लभते: labhate — labh — to obtain (labhate: present middle 3rd sg.)
glossary.स्वकर्मनिरतः: sva-karma-nirataḥ — sva — own (first member); karman — action (second member); ni-ram — devoted to, intent on (nirata: past participle; sva-karma-nirataḥ: 'devoted to his own duty', nom. sg. masc., subject)
glossary.सिद्धिं: siddhim — sidh — success, accomplishment (siddhi: acc. sg. fem., object of vindati)
glossary.यथा: yathā — yathā — how, in what way
glossary.विन्दति: vindati — vid — to find, obtain (vindati: present 3rd sg.)
glossary.तच्छृणु: tat śṛṇu — tad — that (tat: acc. sg. neut., object of śṛṇu; tat+śṛṇu → tacchṛṇu, -t+ś- → -c ch-); śru — to hear (śṛṇu: imperative 2nd sg.)
glossary.यतः: yataḥ — yad — from whom, from which (yataḥ: abl. sg. relative used adverbially)
glossary.प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां: pravṛttiḥ bhūtānām — pra-vṛt — activity, emanation, coming-forth (pravṛttiḥ: nom. sg. fem., subject; -iḥ+bh- → -ir bh-); bhūta — a being (bhūtānām: gen. pl., 'of beings')
glossary.येन: yena — yad — by whom (instr. sg. relative)
glossary.सर्वमिदं: sarvam idam — sarva — all (sarvam: nom. sg. neut., subject); idam — this (idam: nom. sg. neut., in apposition)
glossary.ततम्: tatam — tan — pervaded, spread out, extended (tata: past participle; nom. sg. neut., predicate)
glossary.स्वकर्मणा: sva-karmaṇā — sva — own (first member); karman — action (sva-karmaṇā: 'through his own duty', instr. sg.)
glossary.तमभ्यर्च्य: tam abhyarcya — tad — him (tam: acc. sg. masc., object of abhyarcya, referring to the source just named); abhi-arc — to worship, honor (abhyarcya: gerund, 'having worshipped'; simply joined, final -m unaffected before the vowel)
glossary.मानवः: mānavaḥ — mānava — a human being, a man (nom. sg. masc., subject)
glossary.श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो: śreyān sva-dharmaḥ — śreyas — better (comparative; śreyān: nom. sg. masc., predicate); sva-dharma — one's own dharma, kept untranslated per convention, in this personal-duty sense (sva-dharmaḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before v- → -o)
glossary.विगुणः: viguṇaḥ — vi-guṇa — deficient, imperfectly performed (nom. sg. masc., predicate agreeing with svadharmaḥ)
glossary.परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्: para-dharmāt su-anuṣṭhitāt — para — another's (first member); dharma — dharma, kept untranslated per convention (para-dharmāt: 'than another's dharma', abl. sg., standard of comparison); su — well (prefix); anuṣṭhita — performed, carried out (su-anuṣṭhitāt: 'well-performed', abl. sg., agreeing with paradharmāt; simply joined, dental+s)
glossary.स्वभावनियतं: svabhāva-niyatam — sva-bhāva — one's own nature (first member); ni-yam — fixed, determined, prescribed (niyata: past participle; sva-bhāva-niyatam: 'determined by one's own nature', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with karma)
glossary.कुर्वन्नाप्नोति: kurvan na āpnoti — kṛ — doing (kurvant: present participle; kurvan: nom. sg. masc., 'while doing'; kurvan+na simply joined, doubling the n); na — not; āp — to obtain, incur (āpnoti: present 3rd sg.)
glossary.किल्बिषम्: kilbiṣam — kilbiṣa — sin, fault, guilt (acc. sg. neut., object of āpnoti)
glossary.सहजं: sahajam — saha-ja — born together with [oneself], innate, inborn (sahajam: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with karma)
glossary.कौन्तेय: kaunteya — Kaunteya — son of Kuntī, Arjuna (vocative)
glossary.सदोषमपि: sa-doṣam api — sa- — with, together with (prefix); doṣa — fault, flaw (sa-doṣam: 'though flawed', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with karma; simply joined with api, final -m unaffected before the vowel); api — even, although
glossary.त्यजेत्: tyajet — tyaj — to abandon (tyajet: optative 3rd sg.)
glossary.सर्वारम्भा: sarva-ārambhāḥ — sarva — all (first member); ārambha — an undertaking, a beginning [of action] (sarva-ārambhāḥ: 'all undertakings', nom. pl. masc., subject; sarva+ārambhāḥ → sarvārambhāḥ, a+ā → ā)
glossary.दोषेण: doṣeṇa — doṣa — fault, flaw (instr. sg., 'by fault')
glossary.धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः: dhūmena agniḥ iva āvṛtāḥ — dhūma — smoke (dhūmena: instr. sg.; dhūmena+agniḥ → dhūmenāgniḥ, a+a → ā); agni — fire (agniḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject of the comparison; -iḥ+i- → -ir i-); iva — like, as (iva+āvṛtāḥ → ivāvṛtāḥ, a+ā → ā); ā-vṛ — covered, enveloped (āvṛta: past participle; āvṛtāḥ: nom. pl. masc., predicate agreeing with sarvārambhāḥ)
glossary.असक्तबुद्धिः: asakta-buddhiḥ — a-sakta — not attached, unattached (past participle of sañj negated; first member); buddhi — intellect (a-sakta-buddhiḥ: 'whose intellect is unattached', nom. sg. masc., subject)
glossary.जितात्मा: jita-ātmā — ji — conquered (jita: past participle; first member); ātman — self (jita-ātmā: 'self-conquered', nom. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.विगतस्पृहः: vigata-spṛhaḥ — vi-gata — gone away, departed (first member); spṛhā — longing, craving (vigata-spṛhaḥ: 'from whom craving has departed', nom. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं: naiṣkarmya-siddhim — naiṣkarmya — freedom from the bondage of action, actionlessness (first member); siddhi — attainment, perfection (naiṣkarmya-siddhim: 'the perfection of actionlessness', acc. sg. fem., object of adhigacchati)
glossary.परमां: paramām — parama — supreme (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with siddhim)
glossary.संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति: saṃnyāsena adhigacchati — saṃnyāsa — renunciation (saṃnyāsena: instr. sg., 'through renunciation'); adhi-gam — to reach, attain (adhigacchati: present 3rd sg.; saṃnyāsena+adhigacchati → saṃnyāsenādhigacchati, a+a → ā)
glossary.प्राप्तो: prāptaḥ — pra-āp — attained (prāpta: past participle; nom. sg. masc., subject, 'having attained'; -aḥ before y- → -o)
glossary.ब्रह्म: brahma — brahman — brahman, kept untranslated per convention (acc. sg. neut., object of āpnoti)
glossary.तथाप्नोति: tathā āpnoti — tathā — so, thus (correlative; tathā+āpnoti → tathāpnoti, ā+ā → ā); āp — to reach, attain (āpnoti: present 3rd sg.)
glossary.समासेनैव: samāsena eva — sam-ās — in brief, in summary (samāsa: samāsena: instr. sg.); eva — only, just (samāsena+eva → samāsenaiva, a+e → ai)
glossary.निष्ठा: niṣṭhā — niṣṭhā — steadfastness, the culmination, the final resting-point (nom. sg. fem., subject)
glossary.परा: parā — para — supreme, highest (nom. sg. fem., predicate)
glossary.विशुद्ध्या: viśuddhyā — vi-śuddhi — purity, purification (viśuddhi: instr. sg. fem., 'with purity', treated here as a separate abstract noun beside buddhyā — the vulgate reading, printed here; the BORI critical edition reads viśuddhayā, instr. sg. fem. of the adjective viśuddha, 'purified', agreeing directly with buddhyā, 'with a purified intellect': a real vulgate/BORI variant, not a misprint; see the note)
glossary.युक्तो: yuktaḥ — yuj — joined, disciplined, endowed (yukta: past participle; nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ before dh- → -o)
glossary.धृत्यात्मानं: dhṛtyā ātmānam — dhṛti — steadfastness, firmness, resolve (dhṛtyā: instr. sg., 'with resolve'); ātman — the self (ātmānam: acc. sg., object of niyamya; dhṛtyā+ātmānam → dhṛtyātmānam, ā+ā → ā)
glossary.नियम्य: niyamya — ni-yam — to restrain, control (niyamya: gerund, 'having restrained')
glossary.शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा: śabda-ādīn viṣayān tyaktvā — śabda — sound (first member); ādi — and so on (śabda-ādīn: 'sound and the rest [of the sense-objects]', acc. pl. masc., agreeing with viṣayān); viṣaya — a sense-object (viṣayān: acc. pl. masc., object of tyaktvā; -n+t- → -ṃs t-); tyaj — to abandon (tyaktvā: gerund, 'having given up')
glossary.रागद्वेषौ: rāga-dveṣau — rāga — attraction, passion (first member); dveṣa — aversion, hatred (rāga-dveṣau: 'attraction and aversion', acc. dual masc., object of vyudasya)
glossary.व्युदस्य: vyudasya — vi-ud-as — to cast away, discard (vyudasya: gerund, 'having cast away')
glossary.विविक्तसेवी: vivikta-sevī — vi-vic — secluded, apart, solitary (vivikta: past participle; first member); sevin — resorting to, given to (vivikta-sevī: 'given to solitude', nom. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.लघ्वाशी: laghu-āśī — laghu — light, small (first member); āśin — eating (laghu-āśī: 'eating little', nom. sg. masc., predicate; laghu+āśī → laghvāśī, -u+ā- → -v ā-, yaṇ sandhi)
glossary.यतवाक्कायमानसः: yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ — yam — controlled, restrained (yata: past participle; first member); vāc — speech (second member, surface vāk- before k-); kāya — body (third member); manas — mind (yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ: 'whose speech, body and mind are controlled', nom. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.ध्यानयोगपरो: dhyāna-yoga-paraḥ — dhyāna — meditation (first member); yoga — yoga, kept untranslated per convention (second member); para — intent on, given over to (dhyāna-yoga-paraḥ: 'given over to the yoga of meditation', nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ before n- → -o)
glossary.वैराग्यं: vairāgyam — vairāgya — dispassion, freedom from passion (acc. sg. neut., object of samupāśritaḥ)
glossary.समुपाश्रितः: samupāśritaḥ — sam-upa-ā-śri — resorted to, taken refuge in (samupāśrita: past participle; nom. sg. masc., predicate)
glossary.अहंकारं: ahaṃkāram — ahaṃkāra — egotism, the sense of 'I' (acc. sg. masc., object of vimucya)
glossary.बलं: balam — bala — [aggressive] strength, force (acc. sg. neut., object)
glossary.दर्पं: darpam — darpa — arrogance, pride, conceit (acc. sg. masc., object)
glossary.कामं: kāmam — kāma — desire (acc. sg. masc., object)
glossary.क्रोधं: krodham — krodha — anger (acc. sg. masc., object)
glossary.परिग्रहम्: parigraham — pari-grah — possessiveness, grasping, acquisitiveness (acc. sg. masc., object)
glossary.विमुच्य: vimucya — vi-muc — to abandon, let go of (vimucya: gerund)
glossary.निर्ममः: nirmamaḥ — nir-mama — free from [the sense of] 'mine' (nom. sg. masc., predicate)

about: Chapter 18, Mokṣasaṃnyāsayoga, the Yoga of Liberation and Renunciation, is the Gītā's longest chapter and its summation. Arjuna opens by asking Kṛṣṇa to distinguish saṃnyāsa, the renunciation of action itself, from tyāga, the renunciation of its fruit — and Kṛṣṇa answers that action cannot simply be abandoned, since even the body's maintenance is action; what can and must be given up is attachment to the results. He sorts this renunciation, like everything else in the chapter, into the three guṇas: tyāga done from delusion, from aversion to what is merely difficult, or truly, from duty performed without clinging to its fruit. The same threefold analysis is then run across the five factors that make up any action (the seat of action, the agent, the instruments, the many kinds of effort, and fate), and across knowledge, action, the agent, intellect, steadfastness, and happiness in turn — each shown in its sattva-, rajas-, and tamas-natured forms, from clear-sighted knowledge that sees the one in the many down to the deluded stubbornness or joyless pleasure that mistakes darkness for peace. The chapter then grounds this in the divisions of society: the duties of brahmin, kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra are shown to arise from each person's own nature, and devotion to one's own duty, however imperfect, is declared better than another's performed well — because every action, offered up without attachment, becomes a means to liberation through disciplined intellect and self-mastery, culminating in Kṛṣṇa's supreme instruction to abandon all duties and come to him alone for refuge. The chapter, and the poem, close with instructions on how this teaching is to be transmitted and honored, Arjuna's declaration that his delusion is dispelled and he will act on Kṛṣṇa's word, and Sañjaya's own closing testimony to the wonder of what he has been privileged to hear.
